title: Crime, inland marine, equipment breakdown and farm
summary: One wild month for Tony, his block and Grandma's farm: robbery vs burglary, the two crime triggers, inland marine, a boiler notice and farm A to J.
objectives: Tell robbery, burglary, safe burglary and theft apart
Compare the loss sustained and discovery crime forms
Name the marine classes and match common inland marine forms
Recall equipment breakdown valuation and the farm coverage letters

draw.text: Theft: the umbrella word for all three

beats.text: Monday: a robber threatens Tony at the register.
beats.say: Monday: a robber threatens Tony at the register.

beats.text: The cash. Now!
beats.say: The cash. Now!

beats.text: He takes it. Robbery: taking from a person by harm or a threat of harm, or by an obviously unlawful act they witness.
beats.say: He takes it. Robbery: taking from a person by harm or a threat of harm, or by an obviously unlawful act they witness.

beats.say: Tuesday: a thief hides in the cooler until everyone leaves, then forces the back door to get out with a box of stock. Burglary: unlawful entry or exit. Breaking out counts.

beats.say: Wednesday: the locked safe is pried open and emptied: safe burglary. So is carting off the whole safe. Opened by combination, with no marks? Not safe burglary.

scenes.title: Robbery, burglary or safe burglary?
scenes.src: ISO CR 00 21 11 15, F. defs. 20, 21; IRMI glossary 'burglary'; cp_commercial-03; comm-032, comm-cpa-11, comm-cpa-19

cards.text: A man shows a gun at the counter. The cashier hands over the cash.
cards.why: A person was threatened with harm, and the cash was taken from that person: robbery.

cards.text: A thief hides in the restroom until closing, then kicks open the back door to leave with stock.
cards.why: An unlawful exit counts. A thief who breaks OUT of the premises is still a burglar.

cards.text: Pry marks on the outside of the locked safe door. The cash inside is gone.
cards.why: A locked safe with marks of forced entry on its outside: safe burglary. Opened by combination with no marks, it wouldn't be.

cards.text: A thief grabs cash from the open register while the cashier watches. No threat.
cards.why: An obviously unlawful act the person witnesses is enough for robbery, even with no threat.

cards.text: Thieves wheel the whole safe out of the office and into their van.
cards.why: Taking the safe itself from inside the premises is safe burglary too.

cards.text: Overnight, someone pries open the back door and carries out the sound system. Nobody is there.
cards.why: Theft from inside the premises by unlawful entry, with no one confronted: burglary.

beats.text: Your turn: pick the most specific crime word for each card.
beats.say: Your turn: pick the most specific crime word for each card.

reveal.text: Robbery needs a person. Burglary, unlawful entry or exit. Safe burglary, a forced safe or the whole safe.
reveal.say: Robbery needs a person. Burglary, unlawful entry or exit. Safe burglary, a forced safe or the whole safe.

scenes.title: Seven insuring agreements: money and securities are VIPs
scenes.src: ISO CR 00 21 11 15, A.1-7; adapted from hook mn_comm-12; PSI outline lists the two fraud parts separately

draw.text: 3 Money and securities: theft, disappearance or destruction
4 Other property: robbery or safe burglary only
Money and securities: the same. Other property: robbery only
PSI outline: computer fraud and funds transfer fraud listed apart

beats.text: Tony's crime policy, the 2015 loss sustained form, has seven insuring agreements. Employee Theft: money, securities and other property his employees steal.
beats.say: Tony's crime policy, the twenty fifteen loss sustained form, has seven insuring agreements. Employee Theft: money, securities and other property his employees steal.

beats.text: Back to Tony's bad week. Monday's stolen cash is money, a VIP: inside, money and securities are covered for theft, disappearance or destruction.
beats.say: Back to Tony's bad week. Monday's stolen cash is money, a V I P: inside, money and securities are covered for theft, disappearance or destruction.

beats.text: Tuesday's stock is other property: inside, only robbery of a custodian or safe burglary. So his crime form doesn't cover Tuesday's plain burglary.
beats.say: Tuesday's stock is other property: inside, only robbery of a custodian or safe burglary. So his crime form doesn't cover Tuesday's plain burglary.

beats.text: Outside, with a messenger or armored car company: money and securities, the same. Other property, robbery only.
beats.say: Outside, with a messenger or armored car company: money and securities, the same. Other property, robbery only.

beats.text: Three more: Forgery or Alteration, Computer and Funds Transfer Fraud, and Money Orders and Counterfeit Money.
beats.say: Three more: Forgery or Alteration, Computer and Funds Transfer Fraud, and Money Orders and Counterfeit Money.

scenes.title: Two crime triggers
scenes.src: ISO CR 00 21 11 15, A., E.1.g; discovery: CR 00 22 05 06, E.1.j (CR 00 20 11 15 not seen); mn_comm-13; cp_commercial-04
scenes.plain: Loss sustained: the loss must happen during the policy period. Discovery: it can happen any time, if it's found during the policy period.
scenes.example: The bakery next door cancels its loss sustained policy and buys no other. 9 months later it finds a theft from the policy period: inside the 1-year window.
scenes.exam: Loss sustained: 1 year after cancellation to discover. Discovery: 60 days. Don't swap the tails.

draw.text: Loss sustained: did it HAPPEN during the policy?
Discovery: did I FIND it during the policy?
Loss sustained: found 9 months after canceling

beats.text: Two crime triggers. Loss sustained: did it happen during the policy? Discovery: did I find it during the policy?
beats.say: Two crime triggers. Loss sustained: did it happen during the policy? Discovery: did I find it during the policy?

beats.text: The bakery next door cancels its loss sustained policy, buys no other, and finds a theft from the policy period nine months later. Still inside one year.
beats.say: The bakery next door cancels its loss sustained policy, buys no other, and finds a theft from the policy period nine months later. Still inside one year.

beats.text: Discovery: a loss from any time, and 60 days after cancellation to find it. Don't swap the tails.
beats.say: Discovery: a loss from any time, and sixty days after cancellation to find it. Don't swap the tails.

scenes.q: The dry cleaner on Tony's block buys its first crime policy, a discovery form. Mid-term, it finds a theft from two years before the policy began. No retroactive date applies. Is it covered?
choices: Yes: it was discovered during the policy period
No: it happened before the policy began
Only if found within 60 days after the theft
scenes.why: The discovery form covers loss sustained at any time, as long as it's discovered during the policy period or the 60-day extended period.

beats.text: The dry cleaner buys its first crime policy, a discovery form. Mid-term, it finds a theft from two years before the policy began. Covered?
beats.say: The dry cleaner buys its first crime policy, a discovery form. Mid-term, it finds a theft from two years before the policy began. Covered?

reveal.text: Yes. The discovery form doesn't care when the loss happened, only that it's found during the policy period, or within 60 days after cancellation.
reveal.say: Yes. The discovery form doesn't care when the loss happened, only that it's found during the policy period, or within sixty days after cancellation.

scenes.title: What can inland marine insure?
scenes.src: IMUA 'Nationwide Marine Definition'; hook mn_comm-14; MCL 500.614 (Michigan's marine definition); comm-036

spots.label: Imports and exports: two classes
spots.text: Two classes in one spot: imports and exports, like the loads that cross the Ambassador Bridge.

spots.label: Domestic shipments
spots.text: Domestic shipments, like a truckload of flour rolling up I-75.

spots.label: Bridges and instrumentalities
spots.text: Bridges, tunnels and other instrumentalities of transportation and communication: piers, pipelines, power and phone lines, towers. The Mackinac Bridge counts.

spots.label: Personal property floaters
spots.text: Personal property floater risks, like floaters for personal jewelry, furs, fine arts, stamps and coins, or musical instruments.

spots.label: Commercial property floaters
spots.text: Commercial property floater risks, like floaters for physicians' instruments, theatrical property, film or salesmen's samples, or installation risks.

spots.label: Not marine: buildings
spots.text: Buildings and their fixed contents are not marine risks. In Michigan, the marine insurance statute excludes buildings and their contents too.

beats.text: Inland marine covers goods on the move, bridges and pipelines, and floaters on things like jewelry. The Nationwide Marine Definition lists six classes.
beats.say: Inland marine covers goods on the move, bridges and pipelines, and floaters on things like jewelry. The Nationwide Marine Definition lists six classes.

beats.text: Five spots hold them; the sixth shows what isn't one. Tap each spot.
beats.say: Five spots hold them; the sixth shows what isn't one. Tap each spot.

reveal.text: Six classes, from shipments to floaters. Buildings and their fixed contents aren't marine risks.
reveal.say: Six classes, from shipments to floaters. Buildings and their fixed contents aren't marine risks.

reveal.text: In Michigan, the marine insurance statute excludes them too.
reveal.say: In Michigan, the marine insurance statute excludes them too.

beats.text: Tony's whole block needs inland marine. The dry cleaner is a bailee, holding customers' clothes: bailees customers. The jeweler: jewelers block, for its stock and customers' jewelry.
beats.say: Tony's whole block needs inland marine. The dry cleaner is a bailee, holding customers' clothes: bailees customers. The jeweler: jewelers block, for its stock and customers' jewelry.

beats.say: And the electrician? A contractors equipment floater covers his own tools and machinery; an installation floater, the equipment he's installing. Don't swap them.

scenes.title: Equipment breakdown, once boiler and machinery
scenes.src: EB 00 20 01 13 and EB 99 59 per FC&S (2016), newer edition may exist; RC defined per IRMI glossary; comm-040
scenes.plain: Pays when a business's boilers, machinery, or electrical and communication equipment break down. Its old name: boiler and machinery.
scenes.example: If Tony's boiler breaks down, and his policy has no ACV endorsement, the form values the loss at replacement cost: like kind and quality, no deduction for depreciation.
scenes.exam: Replacement cost, unless the Actual Cash Value endorsement is attached. Coverage on dangerous equipment can be suspended at once by written notice.

beats.text: Equipment breakdown, once called boiler and machinery, covers a breakdown of boilers, machinery, and electrical and communication equipment.
beats.say: Equipment breakdown, once called boiler and machinery, covers a breakdown of boilers, machinery, and electrical and communication equipment.

beats.text: If Tony's boiler breaks down, and his policy has no Actual Cash Value endorsement, the form values it at replacement cost, with no deduction for depreciation.
beats.say: If Tony's boiler breaks down, and his policy has no Actual Cash Value endorsement, the form values it at replacement cost, with no deduction for depreciation.

beats.text: Attach that endorsement, and the valuation switches to actual cash value.
beats.say: Attach that endorsement, and the valuation switches to actual cash value.

scenes.title: Tony's call: the inspector's notice
scenes.src: FC&S 'Equipment Breakdown Coverage Form' (2016), suspension condition (EB 00 20 01 13); a newer edition may exist

draw.text: It's dangerous. Here's my written notice suspending its coverage.

beats.text: Dinner rush at Tony's. The insurer's inspector checks the boiler.
beats.say: Dinner rush at Tony's. The insurer's inspector checks the boiler.

beats.text: It's dangerous. Here's my written notice suspending its coverage.
beats.say: It's dangerous. Here's my written notice suspending its coverage.
beats.speaker: Inspector

beats.text: What should Tony do?
beats.say: What should Tony do?

options.label: Keep it running. The policy's paid up!
options.fail: Once the insurer suspends coverage on dangerous equipment by written notice, a breakdown of that equipment isn't covered.

beats.text: Two days later: bang! Coverage on that boiler was suspended, so the breakdown isn't covered.
beats.say: Two days later: bang! Coverage on that boiler was suspended, so the breakdown isn't covered.

options.label: Relax. Suspension waits 30 days.
options.fail: There's no waiting period: the insurer can suspend coverage on dangerous equipment immediately, by written notice.

beats.text: Tony circles day thirty. On day three, the boiler breaks. The suspension began the moment he got the notice.
beats.say: Tony circles day thirty. On day three, the boiler breaks. The suspension began the moment he got the notice.

draw.text: Suspended at once, by written notice

options.label: Shut it down and get it fixed
options.win: The insurer can suspend coverage on dangerous equipment immediately, by written notice. Tony doesn't bet the pizzeria on it.

beats.text: Smart. Tony shuts it down and calls a repair crew before anything breaks.
beats.say: Smart. Tony shuts it down and calls a repair crew before anything breaks.

reveal.text: Coverage on dangerous equipment can be suspended immediately, by written notice.
reveal.say: Coverage on dangerous equipment can be suspended immediately, by written notice.

scenes.q: Warm-up: under the ISO farm property forms, which of Grandma's animals is NOT livestock?
scenes.why: Livestock means cattle, sheep, swine, goats, horses, mules and donkeys. Chickens are poultry, a separately defined term.

beats.text: Warm-up: Tony's grandma farms in the Thumb.
beats.say: Warm-up: Tony's grandma farms in the Thumb.

beats.text: I've got goats, chickens, mules and swine!
beats.say: I've got goats, chickens, mules and swine!

beats.text: Which one isn't livestock?
beats.say: Which one isn't livestock?

reveal.text: Chickens. Old MacDonald's livestock is seven animals: cattle, sheep, swine, goats, horses, mules and donkeys. The chickens don't count: they're poultry.
reveal.say: Chickens. Old MacDonald's livestock is seven animals: cattle, sheep, swine, goats, horses, mules and donkeys. The chickens don't count: they're poultry.

scenes.title: Grandma's farm, A to J
scenes.src: ISO FP 00 10 09 94 (letters A-G; 2016 forms keep them); FP 00 13 04 16; FL 00 20 per FC&S (2013); mn_comm-15

draw.text: A Dwellings, B Other private structures
C Household personal property, D Loss of use
E: Scheduled farm personal property: each class, its own limit
F: Unscheduled (blanket): one limit. Insure at least 80% of ACV
H Bodily injury and property damage

beats.text: Grandma's farm policy runs A to J. A to D is the farmhouse, lettered like homeowners: dwellings, other private structures, household personal property, loss of use.
beats.say: Grandma's farm policy runs A to J. A to D is the farmhouse, lettered like homeowners: dwellings, other private structures, household personal property, loss of use.

beats.text: E is scheduled farm personal property: each class gets its own limit. F is unscheduled, or blanket: one limit for all, insured to at least 80% of actual cash value. G is other farm structures, like barns.
beats.say: E is scheduled farm personal property: each class gets its own limit. F is unscheduled, or blanket: one limit for all, insured to at least eighty percent of actual cash value. G is other farm structures, like barns.

beats.text: H, I and J are farm liability, mirroring CGL Coverages A, B and C.
beats.say: H, I and J are farm liability, mirroring C G L Coverages A, B and C.

scenes.title: Grandma's call: the cows in the corn
scenes.src: FL 00 20 10 06, Cov. H, I, J per FC&S (2013); FP 00 13 04 16, Cov. F (FC&S 2017); question comm-cpb-45

beats.text: Grandma's cows break through a fence and trample the neighbor's corn.
beats.say: Grandma's cows break through a fence and trample the neighbor's corn.

beats.text: My corn! I'm suing!
beats.say: My corn! I'm suing!

beats.text: Which coverage responds?
beats.say: Which coverage responds?

options.label: Coverage F: it's farm property
options.fail: Coverage F insures Grandma's own farm personal property. The trampled corn belongs to the neighbor.

beats.text: The adjuster shakes his head: F insures Grandma's own farm property. The corn is the neighbor's.
beats.say: The adjuster shakes his head: F insures Grandma's own farm property. The corn is the neighbor's.

options.label: Coverage H: farm liability
options.win: Coverage H pays what she's legally obligated to pay for bodily injury or property damage caused by an occurrence, and defends the suit.

beats.text: Right. Coverage H is her liability coverage for damage to others, and it defends the suit.
beats.say: Right. Coverage H is her liability coverage for damage to others, and it defends the suit.

draw.text: Property damage to others, plus defense

options.label: Coverage J: medical payments
options.fail: Coverage J pays medical expenses for bodily injury. Nobody was hurt; the corn was just flattened.

beats.text: A doctor checks the corn. No patient: J pays medical bills for people who are hurt.
beats.say: A doctor checks the corn. No patient: J pays medical bills for people who are hurt.

draw.text: J: medical bills for injured people

reveal.text: H is bodily injury and property damage liability. I is personal and advertising injury. J is medical payments.
reveal.say: H is bodily injury and property damage liability. I is personal and advertising injury. J is medical payments.

items: Robbery needs a person; burglary needs unlawful entry or exit
Loss sustained: 1 year to discover. Discovery: 60 days
Marine classes exclude buildings and their fixed contents
Equipment breakdown pays replacement cost unless ACV endorsed
Farm: A-D farmhouse, E-G farm property, H-J liability
